correctness.rationale: For every finite field, the quadrics are smooth of Witt index one and the explicit cubic sections are geometrically smooth by distinct complete gradient arguments in characteristics two, three and at least five. Adjunction yields genus four and a canonical embedding; the nonsplit quadric rules out k-rational trigonal pencils (and hyperellipticity), while an explicit k-rational point gives a degree-four pencil via Riemann--Roch. Exact Gröbner-basis computations from verify.py were executed for five representative prime fields; the all-field conclusion uses proof, not sample counts.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected 2022 Faber--Grantham--Howe work poses the all-finite-field gonality-equals-genus existence question as Question 1.3, identifies the genus-four case for fields of size at most four, and suggests a nonsplit-quadric approach over odd fields but does not construct smooth cubic sections uniformly. Its 2020 foundational source provides the canonical quadric classification and a single binary example. The new theorem gives explicit smooth sections simultaneously for every extension in all three characteristic regimes. Targeted literature and research-record searches revealed no theorem whose statement implies the universal construction, though unindexed overlap remains possible.

value.rationale: The published Faber--Grantham--Howe Question 1.3 is motivated by sharp gonality bounds; its genus-four case was described for small fields and an unproved odd-field construction route. This natural existential question is now answered for every finite field by an explicit, characteristic-uniform choice of a nonsplit quadric and smooth cubic section. It is stronger than a routine isolated numerical example and includes all characteristic-two and -three extension fields.
